The test `testExcelHeaderCountLessThanData` in `CSVParserTest` class is failing. The test creates CSV data with an empty header cell and then uses `CSVFormat.EXCEL.withHeader()` to parse the data. The bug report indicates that when there are additional columns not labeled in the CSV data, an `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown due to a duplicate empty header name.

By looking at the `CSVParser.parse` method, it is evident that the `CSVParser` is initialized with the provided `format`, which includes the headers specified by `withHeader` method. The issue seems to be related to how empty header values are handled by `CSVFormat`.

The recent bug report about a `NullPointerException` when having an empty header value could be related to how the empty header value is processed in the `CSVFormat.withHeader` method.

To fix this issue, the `CSVFormat.withHeader` method may need to be adjusted to handle empty header values correctly.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed for this issue.

Please wait a moment.
### Diagnosis

The test case `testExcelHeaderCountLessThanData` in `CSVParserTest` is failing because when using `CSVFormat.EXCEL.withHeader()` to parse CSV data with an empty header cell and additional unlabeled columns, an `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown due to a duplicate empty header name. This indicates an issue with how empty header values are handled by `CSVFormat`.

The `CSVParser.parse` method initializes the `CSVParser` with the provided format, including the headers specified by the `withHeader` method. The bug report and the failing test suggest that the `withHeader` method may not handle empty header values correctly.

### Suggested Fix
- `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.withHeader(java.lang.String...)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
